output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the service's normal range. Over the preceding 26 weeks the average was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks went higher, and investigating them found no fault. The burn-rate page didn't fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard count matches the raw load balancer logs, so it isn't a counting artefact. Booking completion didn't change (41.0% to 41.2%) and support logged no complaints.

The "new pods error at twice the rate" finding doesn't point to v4.18. Every recent rollout shows the same pattern, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. New pods start with an empty cache, and the extra errors are timeouts. That warm-up accounts for only 10–20 errors per rollout, against roughly 2,300 extra errors in the week.

I can't fully rule out a small v4.18, replica or partner-sync effect, but nothing here shows one.

What to do: don't roll back, don't move the replica, and don't mute alerting. Muting would remove the protective page. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to next week. If next week is above the band edge, open an incident then.
